questions.def: 'Haven't' is the correct negative auxiliary verb for 'I' with 'finished'.
questions.question: I ___ finished my homework yet.

questions.def: 'Would' is the correct auxiliary verb to make a polite offer.
questions.question: ___ you like to go to the cinema?

questions.def: The auxiliary verb 'don't' is incorrect; it should be 'doesn't' for 'she'.
questions.question: She don't want to go to the party.

questions.def: 'Is' is the correct form of the auxiliary verb 'be' with 'he'.
questions.question: He ___ going to the store.

questions.def: 'Are' is the correct auxiliary verb to form the present continuous tense.
questions.question: They ___ playing football now.

questions.def: 'Have' is the correct auxiliary verb to use with 'I' in present perfect.
questions.question: I ___ seen that movie before.

questions.def: 'Do' is the correct auxiliary verb to form the question with 'you'.
questions.question: ___ you like coffee?

questions.def: 'Can' is the correct modal auxiliary verb to express ability.
questions.question: She ___ speak English very well.

questions.def: 'Will go' is the correct way to express future tense.
questions.question: He ___ to work tomorrow.

questions.def: 'Have' is the correct auxiliary verb to use with 'they'.
questions.question: They ___ a car.

questions.def: 'Have' is the correct auxiliary verb to start a present perfect question.
questions.question: ___ you seen my keys?

questions.def: 'Went' is the correct past simple form of the verb 'go'. No auxiliary needed.
questions.question: We ___ to the beach yesterday.

questions.def: 'Are' is the correct form of the auxiliary verb 'be' for 'you'.
questions.question: Where ___ you going?

questions.def: 'Would' expresses a polite preference or wish.
questions.question: I ___ like to drink tea.

questions.def: 'Had' is used to form the past perfect tense.
questions.question: They ___ finished dinner when I arrived.

questions.def: 'Can' is a modal auxiliary verb to ask for help.
questions.question: ___ you help me?

questions.def: 'Have' + 'to' expresses obligation for 'you'.
questions.question: You ___ to be quiet in the library.

questions.def: 'Has' is used with 'she' to form the present perfect continuous tense.
questions.question: She ___ been working here for five years.

questions.def: 'Does' is the correct auxiliary verb to use with 'she' in the negative.
questions.question: She ___ like chocolate.

questions.def: 'Will' indicates future tense.
questions.question: They ___ visit us next week.

questions.def: 'Am' is the correct auxiliary verb to use with 'I'.
questions.question: I ___ able to come to the party.

questions.def: 'Is' is the correct auxiliary verb to use with 'there' and singular 'milk'.
questions.question: ___ there any milk in the fridge?

questions.def: 'Won't' is the contraction of 'will not', expressing future negative.
questions.question: We ___ go to the park if it rains.

questions.def: 'Has' is the correct auxiliary verb for 'he' in present perfect.
questions.question: He ___ been to Japan.

questions.def: Singular subjects (she) use 'has' in the present perfect continuous tense.
questions.question: She ___ been studying all day.

questions.def: 'Didn't' is the correct auxiliary for past simple negative.
questions.question: They ___ to the party last night.

questions.def: The correct auxiliary for 'he' is 'Does' in present simple.
questions.question: Do he like to play football every day?

questions.def: 'Am' is the correct form of 'be' for the subject 'I'.
questions.question: I ___ going to the store later.

questions.def: 'Haven't' is the correct auxiliary for 'we' in present perfect negative.
questions.question: We ___ finished our homework yet.

questions.def: 'Would' is used to make a polite offer or request.
questions.question: ___ you like some tea?
